content: The following references provide a comprehensive overview of research, guidelines, and interventions related to drowning prevention, injury control, and disaster risk management: 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) published the Global Report on Drowning: Preventing a Leading Killer in 2014, highlighting the global burden of drowning and strategies for prevention. 2. WHO's 2004 guidelines for conducting community surveys on injuries and violence provide a framework for collecting data to inform prevention strategies. 3. Mello-Jorge and Marques (1985) analyzed violent childhood deaths in Brazil, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions. 4. Rahman et al. (2012) evaluated the cost-effectiveness of an injury and drowning prevention program in Bangladesh, demonstrating its potential impact on reducing mortality. 5. Thompson et al. 6. Depczynski et al. (2009) explored the role of safe play areas in preventing young children from drowning in farm dams in Australia. 7. Iqbal et al. (2007) examined childhood drowning mortality in rural Bangladesh, identifying the magnitude of the problem and proposing solutions. 8. Hyder et al. (2014) developed a framework to address implementation gaps in global drowning prevention interventions, drawing on experiences from Bangladesh. 9. The Saving of Children’s Lives from Drowning project in Bangladesh, as reported by Hyder et al., highlights the effectiveness of community-based interventions. 10. Callaghan et al. (2010) conducted a pilot study on child supervision practices for drowning prevention in rural Bangladesh, testing the feasibility of supervision tools. 11. Islam et al. (2015) presented preliminary findings on the use of playpens to prevent child drowning in rural Bangladesh at the World Conference on Drowning Prevention. 12. Bennett and Linnan (2014) discussed the role of physical barriers in drowning prevention in the second edition of Drowning: Prevention, Rescue, Treatment. 13. Yeh et al. (2011) analyzed injuries associated with cribs, playpens, and bassinets among young children in the U.S., providing insights into product safety. 14. Cordovil et al. (2009) evaluated the efficacy of safety barriers for children, focusing on their effectiveness and the time required to cross them. 15. The Federal Register (2010) outlined safety standards for baby cribs, emphasizing the importance of third-party testing for children’s products. 16. Nixon et al. (1979) conducted an ergonomic study on childproof safety barriers to reduce trauma from environmental hazards. 17. Guevarra et al. (2015) initiated a conversation on child drowning prevention in the Philippines, emphasizing the need for community engagement. 18. Celis (1997) investigated home drowning among preschool-aged children in Mexico, identifying risk factors and prevention strategies. 19. 20. Pearn et al. (2008) discussed the role of safety legislation and public health policy in drowning prevention. 21. Stevenson et al. (2003) examined barriers surrounding private swimming pools and their role in childhood drowning prevention. 22. The WHO's 2008 World Report on Child Injury Prevention provides a global perspective on injury prevention strategies. 23. The WHO Fact Sheet on Drowning (2014) offers key statistics and recommendations for reducing drowning-related deaths. 24. Linnan et al. (2012) presented evidence on child drowning as a significant cause of mortality in lowand middle-income countries, proposing prevention strategies. 25. Stallman et al. (2014) discussed swimming and water survival competence in the context of drowning prevention. 26. Brenner et al. (2009) conducted a case-control study on the association between swimming lessons and childhood drowning, providing evidence for the benefits of swim training. 27. Yang et al. (2007) identified risk factors for childhood drowning in rural regions of a developing country, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions. 28. Rahman et al. (2005) reported on the Bangladesh Health and Injury Survey, focusing on child injury prevention. 29. Mecrow et al. 30. Mecrow et al. (2015) also described children rescuing other children from drowning in rural Bangladesh, highlighting the importance of community-based training. 31. The United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015) emphasized sustainable development and disaster risk management in its global assessment report. 32. Jonkman and Kelman (2005) analyzed the causes and circumstances of flood disaster deaths, providing insights into risk reduction. 33. Haynes et al. (2009) compared shelter-in-place versus evacuation strategies during flash floods, offering guidance for emergency planning. 34. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (2014) synthesized findings on climate change impacts, including flood risks. 35. Hirabayashi et al. (2013) assessed global flood risk under climate change, projecting future vulnerabilities. 36. Hallegatte et al. 37. Chan et al. (2012) explored flood risk in Asia’s urban mega-deltas, identifying drivers, impacts, and responses. 38. Syvitski et al. (2009) discussed the sinking of deltas due to human activities, highlighting the implications for flood risk. 39. The Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030) outlines global priorities for reducing disaster risks. 40. Daellenbach et al. (2015) emphasized the importance of community response planning in disaster risk management. 41. Barbier (2015) valued the storm protection services of estuarine and coastal ecosystems, advocating for ecosystem-based approaches. 42. Dixon et al. (2016) evaluated the effects of river restoration on flood risk and hydrology, providing evidence for nature-based solutions. 43. The American Heart Association (2016) updated its guidelines for cardiopulmonary resuscitation and emergency cardiovascular care, emphasizing best practices. 44. Szpilman et al. (2016) proposed a systematic model of the drowning process, offering a framework for prevention and response. 45. Wallis et al. (2014) reviewed interventions associated with drowning prevention in children and adolescents, identifying effective strategies. 46. Peden et al. (2016) identified research gaps in fatal river drowning through a systematic literature review. 47. Rubin (2011) presented the SwimSafe survival swimming curriculum, emphasizing its role in drowning prevention. 48. Szpilman and Avramidis (2013) conducted a video survey on public perceptions of impactful drowning prevention messages. 49. Frisby and Hill (1991) described a community’s response to childhood drownings, presenting a model for accident prevention. 50. Rahman et al. (2010) evaluated the initial community response to a childhood drowning prevention program in rural Bangladesh, highlighting its feasibility and impact. These references collectively underscore the importance of evidence-based interventions, community engagement, and policy advocacy in addressing drowning and related risks globally.
